test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT the correct characteristic of an I-head combustion chamber used in a petrol engine?

options.text: I-head has higher surface to volume ratio and therefore there is a high amount of heat loss.
I-head has less flame travel length and hence there is a greater freedom from knock.
I-head is superior to an L-head engine at high compression ratios.
I-head has a higher volumetric efficiency from larger valves or valve lifts.

solution:
The correct answer is __Option 1**(I-head has higher surface to volume ratio and therefore there is a high amount of heat loss.)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• I-head combustion chamber__ is widely used in petrol engines due to its compact design and efficiency.
 
• I-head has less flame travel length, leading to greater freedom from knock.
 
• This design is superior to L-head engines at high compression ratios.
 
• It provides higher volumetric efficiency due to larger valves or valve lifts.
 
• Option 1 is NOT correct because I-head does not have a higher surface-to-volume ratio, which would lead to excessive heat loss.
